science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 26 (BS 963), cross-checked against Gaia DR3 XP spectrum, source 5059348952161258624 (20 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12)). The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting. The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,055 K and log g 4.1 (u1 0.404, u2 0.292): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

science.label: Sector 4
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 4.19 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 4 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.07%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.03%, the light's own noise being 0.01%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 4.32 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.15, a width of 0.55 and a fit of 0.99, and in all 6 of the star's sectors together a period of 4.19 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.18, a width of 0.49 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 6 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 8.1% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 4

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#fff7fc, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 106 (July and August 2026): the map's scale, 99.9% to 100.1% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 0.2% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · July and August 2026
